summary: Cook County, MN tower near Brule Lake; reported smoke in 1936 and was later taken down. Undated pages report steel, a stair section and an anchor pad on the site.

facts.design: Steel tower with a cab much larger than typical Minnesota towers and a deck running around the cap (1966 photograph)
facts.status_note: Taken down before 2012 per a forum post; removal date not found. An undated local history page reports steel, a stair section and an anchor pad on the site.

staffing.status: staffed in the 1936 fire season (last record found)

access.note: No closure or permit is described in the sources read. The old trail was hard to find on a 2020 trip (trip report).

visit.trail_note: No standing tower is described at the site. A 2020 trip report found the trail almost impossible to find and unmaintained for about a decade.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (owner listed as USFS in the Cook County survey)

events.note: Survey notes from 1934 and 1958 place a survey station near the center of the tower base
Brule Lake Lookout reported smoke in the 1936 fire season

Brule Lake Lookout and Kelso Lookout reported smoke at about the same time on July 11, after an unusually hot afternoon; comparing the two reports placed the fire near the portage between Gordon and Cherokee lakes
Photograph shows the steel tower with an unusually large cab and a deck around the cap

notes_for_editor: No build date found; the earliest dated record is the 1934 survey note. Removal date not found; the 2012 forum post only says it was taken down years earlier. The kjackson.us page is undated, so the remains description is undated. The 1936 Brule Lake Lookout is taken to be this tower: the MNHS article gives no tower number, and the forum thread calls this tower the Brule Lake Lookout Tower, so the link rests on that name. The 1958 MNHS article calls a 1929 Brule Lake fire the most serious Sawbill fire, but the lookout's role in it is not confirmed, so it is left out. The story is about 315 words of body text.
